api.note: API v1 alone does not establish review-v2 or private Web auth-status capability.

features.note: Both features are additive on review-v2 only. dense-128 raises the finding page from 32 to 128 and stays bounded by the 64 KiB body ceiling Core 0.10.0 serves, and reason-v1 adds a reason to each not_evaluated finding. A request without the header answers the published 32-finding, seven-key document; a header on review-v1, an unknown or repeated token, or an empty part is invalid_request, and a response that enabled a feature echoes the accepted set in the same header.

manuscript.note: v1 and v2 keep their meaning, and an imported v1 or v2 report, a document-mode choice or a semantic decision stays history, not a fresh check. v3 adds per-segment term results for long manuscripts: a saved segment result is reused only when its content hashes, review basis and request inputs all match a live review-v2 basis. v4 keeps v3's 13 top-level keys, the 44 MiB file limit and the canonical bytes, and raises the findings, resolutions and choices limits from 32 to 128 while allowing a reason on a not_evaluated finding; only the label v4 brings those limits, so a v1, v2 or v3 file keeps its 32-item caps and rejects reason. A writer stores the lowest format that holds the content (v1/v2, then v3, then v4). The v4 contract ships in Web 0.4.0, 0.4.1 and 0.4.2 and in Windows 0.6.0, 0.6.1 and 0.6.2, not in Web 0.3.1 or Windows 0.5.1, which reject a v4 file; the shipped-release records below keep the format each release was recorded with.

release.note: v0.4.1 pins the published Core 0.10.1 wheel, whose SHA-256 0b38d3bcf40ee4658e2fdb4423eb5f99620e9d9262614224b5a737aa4cb0529d is the core_binding this bundle records, with core_source_commit dd238303 and the compatibility it declares exact (OCI index sha256:5c68d0d7e45ce67928ddb66c84a83cb75afbdd8b1faef2166c9363dad7768f63, manifest sha256:f94cf6fae5b79388f3c2578e476caa088df9e79604d161fb077163eed27b05c7, config sha256:501746ea792ad53e84116fdbd14e4fe2214f1c68f986e35ad0922389dbadd84e, built by image-bundle run 44697588205). It is a patch release on v0.4.0. The code change (#43) makes a failed shared-pointer send visible instead of silent: both send branches of _point_to_shared_result go through _notice_failed_delivery, so a reuser, including a waiter served the pointer after the same content was queued, receives the failure notice with its resend button while the job stays undelivered, and pressing it or submitting the same content again sends the stored report without another model call. Automatic retry narrows to a send that provably never left: _is_presend_network_error walks the cause chain and accepts only httpx.ConnectError and httpx.ProxyError, so ReadError, RemoteProtocolError, WriteError, a bare NetworkError, BadRequest, Forbidden and TimedOut are not retried, and no retry happens once any chunk has reached the chat. The failure notice splits by outcome: the existing notice says the result was not delivered, and a new uncertain notice says Telegram may have received it and a resend may duplicate, which is the path a ConnectTimeout takes because python-telegram-bot 22.8 raises TimedOut for it rather than NetworkError. Seven test cases cover the two files. The release-prep change (#44) is the Core pin, the package metadata and the docs that describe it, and the tag push produced no duplicate CI run: the only run on this commit that the tag started is the release run itself.

Core moves a minor version, so Telegram moves a minor version; the release-prep change (#42) is the Core pin, the package metadata and the docs that describe what Core now does. The code change is #41: a chat's delivering slot is no longer evicted while a report is being delivered and a full slot set answers the busy notice instead, a member who submits the same text while the source job runs is queued by user and served from the finished report without another model call, a send retry is limited to a network error confirmed not to have reached Telegram, the failure notice carries a resend button guarded against double clicks, expired toasts are bilingual, dead job state is removed, and a tag push no longer triggers a second CI run. /review findings follow Core's wuwaterm-cjk-matcher-v8 basis and its numbering-dot rule, and long /tr paragraph regrouping refuses a crossing break and a merge-plus-split layout. Every LLM request byte, term lock and reference list is identical to Core 0.9.2, and the builder and its terms.db are unchanged, so an existing install keeps the database it built. Kept as history after v0.4.1; the release and its assets are still published. v0.3.1 and earlier remain on the release page.

previous_release.note: v0.4.2 separates long-manuscript state and request handling from the workbench (#48) and is a release prep on top of it (#49). Manuscript state, the live-basis probe and request scheduling move into lib/workbench-model.ts, lib/workbench-persistence.ts and lib/workbench-transport.ts behind the use-semantic-run.ts and use-semantic-requests.ts hooks, so a request started for a manuscript that was then replaced cannot rewrite the new one, an obsolete semantic review outcome is ignored, and a translation survives a change of review basis. contracts/workbench-state/cases.json fixes six shared state cases (opened-before-live-basis, matching-live-basis, changed-matcher-basis, local-target-edit, direction-changed and alignment-changed) that the Windows client replays against the same model; Windows 0.6.2 and Web dfa3cf40 passed those six cases and 13 bidirectional manuscript checks together (Windows #34, Web #48). The manuscript formats, the BFF response shape, the /v1 proxy, the database schema, the dependencies, the hosting configuration and the Core and Windows contract pins are those of 0.4.1; the release prep moves only package.json and package-lock.json. The docs/self-hosting.md packaged inside both archives still names the older Core integration commit 64e293cf, so the Web instruction link of that checkout named the corrected guide on Web main (26144b40, #50) instead.
